steps.content: I am the Brahmi script. Extremely ancient, highly significant, and very dear!
I am the Brahmi script.
steps.subtitle: Extremely ancient, highly significant, and very dear!

steps.content: I am the script created by the first Tirthankara, Maharaja Shri Rishabhadeva.
He created me while teaching his daughter Brahmi.
Along with Brahmi, Maharaja Shri Rishabhadeva also taught 'Numerology' to his other daughter, Sundari.
Both of them highly propagated the knowledge given by Lord Shri Rishabhadeva.
Why was I named 'Brahmi Lipi'? The knowledge of this script was imparted to the general public by Brahmi, hence I was named 'Brahmi script'.

steps.title: I am not a language!
steps.content: Remember that I am not a language, just a writing system.
1. "The way we speak is called 'language'." For example — Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati, Kannada, Odia, Punjabi, English, etc.

2. "The medium through which a language is written is called 'script'." For example — Hindi-Devanagari, Bengali-Bengali, Telugu-Telugu, Tamil-Tamil, Gujarati-Gujarati, Kannada-Kannada, Odia-Odia, Punjabi-Gurmukhi, English-Latin, etc.

steps.title: My Specialty
steps.content: I am originally the script of the 'Prakrit language'.
But you can use me to write any language just like Devanagari or Latin/Roman script.
And yes, I will tell you a secret. You can make me your secret script and hide all your secrets from ordinary people.

steps.title: My Importance
steps.content: My vowels and consonants are exactly like Devanagari (Hindi). I can connect you directly to Tirthankara Shri Rishabhadeva.
So do not leave my side.

You are truly curious and eager to learn, which is why you have reached this stage of this unique journey.

Hearty congratulations and best wishes!
I will try my best to connect you directly to Tirthankara Rishabhadeva Maharaj because now you only have me as the true creation of the Tirthankara Lord.
I know what you are thinking. We call the texts we have 'Jinavani', which means the divine sound of Lord Jinendra.
So today we do not have the direct form of the Tirthankara Lord with us.
Yes absolutely! You spoke correctly. But think once, we consider and worship the texts we have as Jinavani.
The divine sound of the Lord was woven by the Gandharas, and only a little has reached us through the direct visual tradition of the Acharyas.
But that is not the direct Jinavani, it is Jinavani in the form of tradition.

After the holy Nirvana of Lord Shri Rishabhadeva, crossing a boundless time journey of one Koda-Kodi Sagar, I am present before you today — with the sacred memories of endless eras, the unbroken Ganges of knowledge, and the divine heritage of Lord Rishabhadeva.
So you understand now; how I am the direct creation of the Tirthankara Lord.
Wow! This means you can learn the entire Brahmi script in a very short time.
Come! Let's begin from the beginning.

matraIntro.text1: When vowels are written alone, they have their own distinct symbol, but when they join with a consonant, they become a matra symbol.
matraIntro.text2: Matra: A short form of a vowel that attaches to a consonant and changes its sound.

matraTable.note: No matra — the consonant inherently contains the 'a' sound

rules.title: Independent Vowels
rules.description: When vowels are at the beginning of a word or alone, they take their independent form.

rules.title: Matra Symbols
rules.description: When a vowel comes after a consonant, it becomes a matra and is written attached to the consonant.

rules.title: Placement of Matra
rules.description: Matras can be placed in different positions: top, bottom, front, back.

rules.title: Special Attention
rules.description: The shape and placement of matras in the Brahmi script is slightly different from Devanagari — observe, practice, and recognize.

vyanjan.content: Congratulations! You have reached this far wonderfully – your hard work and curiosity are commendable!
Level-up Alert! You have learned vowels and matras with such dedication that we are now giving you a bonus module. Bonus Gift:
You will now get a special introduction to a consonant right before the lesson! This consonant will help you understand how matras combine with any consonant to form words.
How will it work? Select a consonant of your interest. We will teach you its form, pronunciation, writing, and combination with matras.

vyanjan.prompt: Select — Which group do you want?

vyanjan._devNote_groupNote: Placing the tongue near the teeth

vyanjan.instruction: Instructions: Select your marked consonant below — and soon start learning its introduction, pronunciation, and combination with matras.

vyanjan.content: Bonus: Consonant Introduction – "KA" (𑀓)
vyanjan.subtitle: Welcome! You have chosen the "क" consonant!
vyanjan.note: Today we will learn – its form, pronunciation and reading/writing with matras

vyanjan.content: In Brahmi script, the form of "KA" is: 𑀓. Pronunciation: ka (e.g. – kamal, kaksha)
vyanjan.drill: Try it – speak loudly: क… क… क

vyanjan.title: Without Matra
vyanjan.content: When "ka" is alone → 𑀓 (sound: ka). Without matra = only consonant sound + 'a' vowel is inherently attached.

matra.content: When vowels are written alone, they have their own distinct symbol, but when they join with a consonant, they become a matra symbol.
Matra: A short form of a vowel that attaches to a consonant and changes its sound.

matra.note: No matra — the consonant inherently contains the 'a' sound

matra.title: Independent Vowels
matra.description: When vowels are at the beginning of a word or alone, they take their independent form.

matra.title: Matra Symbols
matra.description: When a vowel comes after a consonant, it becomes a matra and is written attached to the consonant.

matra.title: Placement of Matra
matra.description: Matras can be placed in different positions: top, bottom, front, back.

matra.title: Special Attention
matra.description: The shape and placement of matras in the Brahmi script is slightly different from Devanagari — observe, practice, and recognize.
matra.guidance: Guidance: Observe carefully, practice, and recognize.
